root_cause.text: The HFS mount path leaked the filesystem-private `sb->s_fs_info` object because error cleanup after `sget_fc()`/`setup_bdev_super()` failure no longer freed the newly allocated `hfs_sb_info`, and `hfs_mdb_put()` also stopped freeing `HFS_SB(sb)` and clearing `sb->s_fs_info`.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE says that if `setup_bdev_super()` fails “after a new superblock has been allocated by sget_fc(), but before hfs_fill_super() takes ownership of the filesystem-specific s_fs_info data it was leaked,” and the patch fixes this by adding `hfs_kill_super()` to `kfree(hsb)` after `kill_block_super(sb)`, while the diff removes `kfree(HFS_SB(sb)); sb->s_fs_info = NULL;` from `hfs_mdb_put()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Return -EIO immediately when reading the HFS MDB fails instead of using the generic cleanup path.
intent_record.what: In hfs_mdb_get(), the error path after a failed sb_bread512() call was changed from jumping to the common out label to immediately returning -EIO.
intent_record.how: When reading the HFS master directory block fails, the function now explicitly reports an I/O error instead of falling through the shared cleanup path, making the failure return value deterministic for this read error case.

intent_record.intent_summary: Return a proper I/O error directly on HFS MDB parsing failures and invalidate bad allocation block sizes with explicit cleanup.
intent_record.what: In hfs_mdb_get(), two error paths were changed from jumping to cleanup labels to returning -EIO directly: the hfs_part_find() failure now returns -EIO instead of goto out, and an invalid allocation block size now brelse(bh) and returns -EIO instead of goto out_bh.
intent_record.how: These changes make the function immediately fail with a consistent I/O error when partition discovery fails or the MDB allocation block size is invalid, while explicitly releasing the buffer head in the bad-size case before returning.

intent_record.intent_summary: Simplify and clarify hfs_mdb_get() error handling by returning -EIO directly on blocksize, read, and signature validation failures.
intent_record.what: In hfs_mdb_get(), two failure paths that previously jumped to cleanup labels were changed to immediate `return -EIO;` statements: one when `sb_set_blocksize()` fails, and one when `sb_bread512()` fails. The superblock magic check was also expanded from a bare conditional jump to an explicit block that calls `brelse(bh)` before returning `-EIO` when `mdb->drSigWord` is not `HFS_SUPER_MAGIC`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now exits directly with an I/O error on these invalid or unreadable metadata cases instead of relying on later cleanup labels. This preserves the same failure outcome while making the error handling more explicit, and it ensures the buffer is released immediately on the bad superblock signature path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Return a proper I/O error immediately when bitmap allocation fails in hfs_mdb_get().
intent_record.what: In hfs_mdb_get(), the failure path after kzalloc(8192, GFP_KERNEL) was changed from `goto out;` to an immediate `return -EIO;` when `HFS_SB(sb)->bitmap` allocation fails.
intent_record.how: If allocating the bitmap buffer fails, the function now exits right away with an I/O error instead of jumping to the shared cleanup path. This makes the allocation failure explicitly report `-EIO` to the caller at that point.

intent_record.intent_summary: Return a proper I/O error immediately when reading the volume bitmap fails.
intent_record.what: In `hfs_mdb_get(struct super_block *sb)`, the error path after `sb_bread()` fails was changed from `goto out;` to `return -EIO;`.
intent_record.how: When reading the volume bitmap block fails, the function now immediately returns an I/O error instead of jumping to the საერთო cleanup path. This makes the failure explicitly reported as `-EIO` at the point of detection.

intent_record.intent_summary: Return -EIO immediately when opening the HFS extent or catalog tree fails.
intent_record.what: In hfs_mdb_get(), the failure handling for hfs_btree_open() when opening the extent tree and catalog tree was changed from jumping to the shared out label to immediately returning -EIO.
intent_record.how: If either tree cannot be opened, the function now exits right away with an I/O error instead of continuing to a cleanup path via out. This makes the failure return explicit at the point of error and preserves the same error indication while avoiding any later code path that might have followed the goto target.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove obsolete error-handling labels and cleanup code from `hfs_mdb_get()`.
intent_record.what: The diff removes the `out_bh:` and `out:` error-handling labels at the end of `hfs_mdb_get(struct super_block *sb)`, along with the `brelse(bh);`, `hfs_mdb_put(sb);`, and `return -EIO;` statements associated with those labels.
intent_record.how: This changes the function so it no longer has those local cleanup-and-fail paths in that location; execution now falls through to the existing successful `return 0;` path, implying the removed labels are no longer reachable from the shown code.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove an unnecessary null guard so `hfs_mdb_put()` always performs MDB cleanup through the HFS superblock state.
intent_record.what: The early return guard `if (!HFS_SB(sb)) return;` was removed from `hfs_mdb_put(struct super_block *sb)`, so the function now always proceeds to close the B-trees using `HFS_SB(sb)->ext_tree` and `HFS_SB(sb)->cat_tree`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, `hfs_mdb_put()` no longer skips cleanup when `HFS_SB(sb)` is null; it will attempt to access the HFS superblock state unconditionally. This changes behavior by removing a safety check and makes the function rely on callers only invoking it when HFS-private superblock data is present.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove explicit freeing and nulling of the HFS superblock private data from hfs_mdb_put().
intent_record.what: Two lines were removed from hfs_mdb_put(): the call to kfree(HFS_SB(sb)); and the subsequent assignment sb->s_fs_info = NULL;.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function no longer explicitly frees the superblock filesystem-private info structure or clears the superblock's fs_info pointer during this cleanup path. The remaining cleanup still frees the bitmap and unloads the NLS table, so this change alters ownership/lifetime handling for HFS_SB(sb) and may shift freeing of that structure to another code path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix HFS superblock teardown to free filesystem-private state after killing the block superblock.
intent_record.what: A new static function `hfs_kill_super(struct super_block *sb)` was added. It retrieves `struct hfs_sb_info *hsb = HFS_SB(sb)`, calls `kill_block_super(sb)`, and then frees `hsb` with `kfree(hsb)`. The `hfs_fs_type.kill_sb` callback was changed from `kill_block_super` to `hfs_kill_super`.
intent_record.how: At unmount/superblock teardown time, HFS now performs the normal block-super cleanup and also releases the HFS-specific superblock private data. This prevents the filesystem's per-superblock allocation from persisting after teardown.

consistency_review.core_intent: Handle HFS MDB-related failures by returning explicit I/O errors and cleaning up invalid allocation block sizing.
Simplify hfs_mdb_get() by removing obsolete error-handling labels and consolidating failure paths into direct error returns.
Fix HFS superblock teardown and related MDB cleanup so filesystem-private state is always released correctly after the block superblock is killed.

relevance_review.reason: The changes focus on HFS MDB read/parse error handling and block-size validation, but the root cause is a memory leak from missing cleanup of hfs_sb_info and sb->s_fs_info after mount/setup failures. This group does not address that cleanup path.

The root cause is an HFS mount cleanup leak after failure paths in hfs_mdb_get()/mount setup. This group explicitly changes hfs_mdb_get() error handling by removing cleanup labels and consolidating failure returns, which directly affects the faulty cleanup behavior tied to the leak.

This change only alters error handling for bitmap allocation failure in hfs_mdb_get() by returning an I/O error sooner. It does not address the leak of hfs_sb_info/sb->s_fs_info on mount/setup failure or the missing cleanup in hfs_mdb_put().
The change only makes volume bitmap read failures return a proper I/O error. It does not address the leaked hfs_sb_info / sb->s_fs_info cleanup issue in mount error paths or hfs_mdb_put().

The change only alters error handling for failing to open HFS extent/catalog trees by returning -EIO. It does not address the leaked hfs_sb_info/sb->s_fs_info cleanup path described in the root cause.

The changes directly match the root cause: they restore proper HFS superblock teardown and MDB cleanup so the filesystem-private sb->s_fs_info/HFS_SB state is freed and cleared on failure or teardown, fixing the leak.

The group directly matches part of the root cause: it removes the freeing and nulling of HFS superblock private data in hfs_mdb_put(), which is specifically described as contributing to the leaked sb->s_fs_info object.

candidates.rationale: This is the explicit free of the filesystem-private superblock object. Its removal means the allocated hfs_sb_info is no longer released during teardown, directly causing the leak described in the root cause.

Clearing s_fs_info after freeing the private state prevents dangling references and is part of the cleanup that was removed. Without this cleanup, the mount path can retain leaked/invalid private state.

This error-path cleanup call was the mechanism that released MDB and superblock-private state on setup failure. Removing it from the failure path leaves the newly allocated hfs_sb_info unreleased after sget_fc()/setup_bdev_super() errors.

This guard allowed hfs_mdb_put() to return early when private state was absent, but in the buggy path it also contributed to skipping cleanup of filesystem-private data, which the fix addresses by ensuring cleanup always runs.

vuln_statements.explanation: This error-path cleanup call released the HFS superblock-private state when mount setup failed. Its removal from the failure path caused the newly allocated hfs_sb_info to leak after sget_fc()/setup_bdev_super() errors.
This explicitly freed the filesystem-private superblock object. Without it, the hfs_sb_info allocated for the mount is not released during teardown, leaking sb->s_fs_info.
This cleared the superblock's private-data pointer after freeing it. Removing it leaves the filesystem-private state associated with the superblock and contributes to the leak of sb->s_fs_info.

This null guard allowed hfs_mdb_put() to return early instead of always cleaning up HFS superblock-private data. In the buggy mount path, that contributed to skipping release of the allocated hfs_sb_info.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet contains the HFS mount-time cleanup path and the MDB teardown path, which are directly relevant to the leak described. In `hfs_mdb_get()`, on failures it does `goto out;` and then `out: hfs_mdb_put(sb); return -EIO;`, but `hfs_mdb_put()` only says `/* free the B-trees */` followed by `hfs_btree_close(...)` and buffer releases (`brelse(HFS_SB(sb)->mdb_bh); brelse(HFS_SB(sb)->alt_mdb_bh);`). There is no freeing of a filesystem-private `sb->s_fs_info` / `HFS_SB(sb)` object and no clearing of `sb->s_fs_info`. That matches the root cause: the cleanup path does not free the newly allocated HFS superblock info structure. The code also has no fix for this yet, since there is no `kfree(HFS_SB(sb))`, no `sb->s_fs_info = NULL`, and no analogous error-unwind cleanup for the private superblock allocation.
